Definition: Artachshasta (or Artaxerxes), a title (rather than name) of several Persian kings
BiblicalUsage: Artaxerxes is a title, not one man's name, worn by several kings of Persia, and the books of Ezra and Nehemiah name it for the kings who let the Jews go home. Artaxerxes gives Ezra a letter with silver and gold for the temple, and in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes Nehemiah the cupbearer asks leave to rebuild the wall of Jerusalem.
TheologicalSignificance: A king's title that turns up on both sides of the return tells me God moves the hearts of kings: the same throne that stopped the work lets it go on, and the letters of a Persian king carry the silver for God's house.
